comments.content: The parametrized test_mark_plant_dead reuses the exact same plant_id 'TO-2026-001' for both parameter sets. Since each call to the /dead endpoint mutates the plant state (marking it dead), the second parametrized invocation will operate on an already-dead plant and likely receive a 400 response instead of the expected 200. This introduces test order/state dependency and will cause the test to fail or flake.

mark_plant_dead uses bare function parameters (death_date, death_reason, death_comment) which FastAPI treats as required query parameters for the PATCH endpoint. This violates REST conventions for updates (prefer request body), bypasses Pydantic schema validation and OpenAPI documentation for the payload, and can cause encoding issues for fields like death_comment. Use a Pydantic model (e.g., PlantDeathRequest) with Body() instead.

Also, death_date only checks strptime format; no range validation (future dates, before planting date etc.) - relies on later service but prompt should be robust.

Client-side validation in markPlantDeadApiPlantsPlantIdDeadPatch trims inputs and throws a synchronous Error('death_date and death_reason are required and non-empty') if empty. This does not match the defined response type (which includes 400/404/422 error variants) or the pattern used by other functions (which always return {data, status, headers} even for errors). Callers expecting to inspect status for errors will receive uncaught exceptions instead.
